Motif Kit SDK 4.0 · motif-kit@4 · Motif 8.0

What changed in the SDK

Four additions asked for in one release: vector graphics and typography, layer stacks with blend modes, independent speed and direction, and a Sequencer that calls shaders from your library at points of the loop. The SDK, the app that hosts it, the tools and the docs all moved together.

Format motif-kit@4SDK 3.0 → 4.0App 7.1.1 → 8.0Older kits unchangedLibrary 89 → 101 styles
RequirementsSequencerLayer stacksSpeed & directionVector & typeToolingVerificationLimits

The four requests, and where they landed

Each request became a concrete, opt-in feature of the new motif-kit@4 format. Existing kits do not change.

RequestDelivered
Vector graphics and typographyA distance-shape library in GLSL, svg inputs baked to distance fields, and distance fields for live text inputs, so outlines, glows and echoes stay exact at any scale.
Image layer stacking, up to 3, layer modes, independent motion and opacity"stack": { "layers": 3 }: three media layers per shader, 12 blend modes, opacity, offset, scale, rotation, edge mode and motion on every layer.
Independent speed; forward, backward, randomWhole cycles per loop plus forward, backward, ping-pong and random, loop-exact. Video layers are seeked by the same playhead.
Sequencer that invokes library shaders at points of the loopA Sequencer layer in the app: a lane timeline of cues, a cue editor, sequences shipped inside kits, at most 4 shaders running at once.
The app had to change too. Motif 7.1.1 could not compile the new GLSL, bake vectors, drive video by a playhead or render a Sequencer, so the SDK work shipped together with Motif 8.0. The new kit format is motif-kit@4; Motif 7 and earlier reject it cleanly by its format string.

Sequencer new

More looks than four layers, without more than four shaders at once. A cue plays a style for part of the loop, then ends.

Edit on the timeline

Drag a cue to move it across the loop and lanes, drag an edge to resize, or use arrow keys, Shift to resize and Delete on a focused cue.

Per-cue control

Any style from the library, how many times it plays, direction, blend, opacity, fades, chance, seed, mute, and the style's own settings.

Safe by construction

Cues start and end invisible, close on themselves, and the planner skips the dimmest cue if more than 4 overlap. Same code runs in the page and the render worker.

Shipping a sequence in a kit

{ "format": "motif-seq@1", "id": "showcase", "name": "Showcase", "loop": 12, "bpm": 120, "maxActive": 3,
  "cues": [
    { "id": "bed",   "style": "swirl", "at": 0,    "len": "6s", "lane": 0 },
    { "id": "rings", "style": "rings", "at": "1s", "len": "3s", "lane": 1, "cycles": 2, "blend": "screen" },
    { "id": "scan",  "style": "scan",  "at": "2s", "len": "1.5s", "lane": 2, "repeat": { "every": "5s", "count": 2 } } ] }

Times accept a fraction of the loop, "3/16", "25%", "1.5s" or "2b" (beats). Validation rejects more than 4 overlapping cues, unknown styles and bad times, and warns about gaps. A sequence shows up in the layer's Load a sequence menu.

Layer stacks new

One style can composite up to three images or clips. The app generates the media slots and a control block per layer; every control is an ordinary channel, so keyframes, locks, Mutate, audio mapping and presets work.

styles: [{
  "id": "image-stack",
  "stack": { "layers": 3,
    "labels": ["Back","Middle","Front"],
    "defaults": [{ "blend": "normal" },
                 { "blend": "screen" },
                 { "blend": "overlay" }] },
  ...
}]
// GLSL
vec4 c = vec4(base, 1.0);
c = L_stack(c, uv);   // all layers, own blend + opacity
// or one layer at a time:
vec4 a = L_get1(uv);  float o = L_opacity(1);

12 blend modes

Normal, multiply, screen, overlay, soft light, hard light, add, darken, lighten, difference, exclusion, colour dodge (W3C formulas).

Per-layer motion

Offset, scale, rotation, edge mode (clip, repeat, mirror, extend), cycles per loop, direction and travel.

Video-aware

With cycles above 0 a clip plays forward, backward, ping-pong or in random round trips, frame-exact in exports.

Not counted as params

Generated controls do not use up the 32-parameter limit (128 uniforms per style in total).

Speed and direction new

Every layer and svg has Cycles / loop (a whole number) and Direction. Whole cycles are what keep every loop seamless: frame 0 always equals the frame at the loop length.

Forward

k·phase. Scrolls whole tiles, so it wraps cleanly.

Backward

−k·phase. The same, reversed.

Ping-pong

0 → 1 → 0, k round trips per loop.

Random

Each round trip goes out the forward or backward way, picked by a seeded hash. Deterministic.

The JavaScript playhead matches the shader's (8,192 samples, every random direction agreeing), and that is what seeks video: a clip driven backward at time t equals the same clip driven forward at loop length minus t. Slower motion comes from a longer loop or lower tempo, not from fractional speeds, which would break the seam.

Vector graphics and typography new

Shapes and type are baked into signed distance fields once, so each frame is one texture read and edges stay sharp at any size.

// shapes, no host support needed
float d = opSub(sdRoundBox(uv, vec2(0.3,0.12), 0.04),
                sdCircle(uv, 0.08));
return vpaint(d, u_a0, u_ink, 0.008, u_a1, 0.05);
// inputs in the manifest
"capabilities": ["vector", "text"],
"inputs": [
  { "id": "mark", "type": "svg", "src": "assets/mark.svg" },
  { "id": "title", "type": "text", "sdf": true, "lines": [...] }
]
// GLSL: vec_mark(uv)   textDist_title(i, q)

Shape toolkit

sdCircle sdRoundBox sdRing sdNgon sdTriangle sdStar sdArc sdBezier, boolean and rounding operators, and vfill vstroke vglow vpaint.

SVG stays data

Parsed by a small scanner and drawn with Path2D, never rendered by the browser. Scripts, images and external references are rejected, and a new vector capability is shown at install.

Type on the existing atlas

No second text system: "sdf": true adds a distance field to the text inputs introduced in SDK 3.0.

Tooling, validation and docs

Everything around the format moved too.

Validator and sandbox

Stacks, svg files, distance fields and sequences are validated with file-level messages. Generated controls cannot clash with yours, hostile SVG parses in linear time (fuzz-tested), and the existing static GLSL analysis, capability approval, canary and quarantine cover @4.

CLI

motif-kit new --example stack|vector|sequence, motif-kit seq (validate and print which cues play when), motif-kit prelude --v4, and a much richer preview.

Preview that tests the new features

Bakes SVG and distance fields exactly as the app does, feeds each stack layer its own test card, runs a motion-seam test in all four play modes, and renders every sequence (8 frames, loop-tested).

Schemas and docs

New motif-kit-4.schema.json, the project schema gains the Sequencer layer, and the docs add a kit-format-4 spec plus updates to versioning, sandbox and text inputs.

Three reference kits

  • Stack Lab: two layer-stack styles.
  • Vector Type: Shape Field, Logo Reveal, Type Poster.
  • Sequence Demo: six small styles and two sequences (Showcase, Beat Reel).

They are bundled in the app, shipped as .motifkit files, and available as editable sources and as motif-kit new --example templates.

Verification

Measured on software GL in headless Chromium, from the extracted package.

89 / 89Motif 7.1.1 styles render identical pixels in Motif 8
20existing kits validate byte-identically (output, warnings, analysis)
12 + 67unit tests and browser checks passing
0console errors across the browser suite
  • A one-cue Sequencer is pixel-identical to the style drawn directly (kit shaders).
  • Worker and main-thread renders of a Sequencer layer agree.
  • Every new style closes its loop, including all four play modes with speed on.
  • The shader and JavaScript playheads agree on every random direction.

Not run: a full MP4 export, a real GPU, Safari and Firefox.

Known limits and next steps

Limits in 8.0

  • SVG: paths and basic shapes only; colours are ignored; a user cannot attach their own SVG yet.
  • No per-letter kinetic type yet.
  • A Sequencer cue cannot carry its own image or text.
  • Distance fields round very sharp corners at extreme magnification.
  • Bundled fonts were deliberately not added: kits stay text-only.

Suggested for 8.1

  • Per-glyph type animation from a glyph atlas.
  • Multi-channel distance fields for razor corners.
  • User-attached SVG on svg inputs.
  • Sequencer macros and beat-triggered cues.
  • Per-cue media and text.
